entry_state: A group result depends on exact legal books, source revisions, currencies, control intervals and matched transactions. Eliminating an intragroup monetary balance does not remove its currency result; settlement facts determine profit versus net-investment OCI. Hyperinflation first restates dated nonmonetary amounts, income and capital while preserving nominal monetary balances, then translates; first-application tax and prior comparatives require their own ordering. The next question is whether a quoted exchange rate is actually accessible for the specified purpose and date.
exit_state: Exchangeability is assessed for the currency direction, date, purpose and obtainable amount, using enforceable mechanisms rather than intention. Failure requires a supported orderly-exchange estimate, not automatic adoption of an observable or later quote. Initial application has distinct retained-earnings or translation-reserve origins and unchanged comparatives. These documentary extensions require a successor group profile; they do not silently extend the existing closed exchange contract.

findings.judgment: The chapter ends with the inspected 2024/2862 amendment and its effective-date distinction, avoiding extrapolation of the older temporary-exchangeability rule. The 5-available/1000-needed illustration supplies evidence for judgment rather than inventing a numeric test. Purpose-specific inability to remit an investment is not answered by an import rate. The admitted 0.08 estimate gives translated net assets 80 while other observed rates give 100/90, but arithmetic alone does not validate the estimate. Initial-application payable and translation adjustments have separate equity origins; disclosure and unsupported estimation remain explicit. The closing paragraph requires an extended profile before software support can be claimed.
